reimbursement_policies.evidence: The policy does not name this DRG, but it does exclude admissions for substance abuse and rehabilitation from the inpatient readmissions rule. The general readmission denial logic applies only to covered inpatient DRG or case-rate facilities and does not separately reimburse unplanned 30-day same or related readmissions.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Opioid Use Disorder (OUD) Services and Medication Assisted Treatment (MAT)
reimbursement_policies.evidence: The policy does not address DRG-based inpatient reimbursement for this alcohol/drug dependence DRG. It instead covers medically necessary opioid use disorder treatment and medication assisted treatment services, including specific CPT/HCPCS billing and OTP rules.

Off-topic for the requested DRG pattern. This policy addresses medically necessary urine drug testing and does not set reimbursement rules for the DRG/residential behavioral health scenario described.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Outpatient Behavioral Health & Substance Use Disorder

recommended_action.description:
Recommendation 1: For California cesarean-delivery inpatient claims paid under 'DRG' or 'Case rate', apply a readmission edit only when the episode satisfies Elevance’s pairing conditions 'within 30 days of discharge', for 'same or related diagnoses', and within the policy’s '30-day readmission window', using the listed facility linkage conditions 'same facility agreement', 'same tax identification number', and 'common ownership'; exclude 'substance abuse admissions', 'rehabilitation admissions', 'cancer admissions', 'transplant admissions', 'transfer from another facility', 'against medical advice', 'planned readmissions', and 'leave of absence'. Apply to California. Exempt: substance abuse admissions, rehabilitation admissions, cancer admissions, transplant admissions, transfer from another facility, against medical advice, planned readmissions, leave of absence.

Recommendation 2: In California cesarean-delivery episodes, deny or pend any time-based professional procedure claim unless the documentation includes 'recorded start and stop times', 'timely entry should not exceed 30 days', the 'signature date within 30 days of service', and 'Each entry must include author identification of the physician, other qualified health care provider, or supervising provider'; carve out 'provider, state, or federal contracts and/or requirements'. Apply to California. Exempt: provider, state, or federal contracts and/or requirements.
